recipes.name: Fisherman's Catch Chowder
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) can whole peeled tomatoes, mashed

steps.text: In a slow cooker, stir together the cod, tomatoes, clam juice, onion, celery, carrots, wine, parsley, rosemary, and salt. Cover, and cook on Low 7 to 8 hours or on High 3 to 4 hours.
One hour prior to serving, mix flour, butter, and light cream in a small bowl. Stir into the slow cooker until the fish mixture is thickened.

raw_recipe.headline: Fisherman's Catch Chowder
raw_recipe.description: A fisherman's dream soup with an abundance of vegetables, rosemary, and parsley.

review.reviewBody: We loved this dish. Used Halibut and it turned out super yummy... Even our three year old liked it. My husband added mushrooms and garlic.. Can't wait to have it again.

This was yummy! I had some broiled northern pike I needed to use. It was already broiled with lemon, olive oil, crushed garlic, and sliced ginger. Since it was already cooked, I did not get out the crock-pot, I simply threw all ingredients in a large pot and simmered for 30 minutes. I did try it both with the cream and without. It was good both ways, but we opted to leave out the cream for the majority of the soup. I didn't use the flour to thicken because as others mentioned, it was already very thick. I did throw in the butter though! It was very tasty and a great way to use up the pike.

I needed a dish for ocean perch, saw this recipe and felt confident it would be good based on all the positive reviews. The dish was fantastic, I just need to experiment with the seasoning because it needs a boost of something, likely salt. Since there are already so many helpful and similar tips to consider, I’m just going to share a few things I haven’t seen yet. 1) I used Pinot Grigio, which provided a great fragrance and flavor. 2) No clam juice at my store so I used 8 oz chicken broth + 1tbsp fish sauce. 3) Cooked in crockpot on high for about 1hr 45 min. If you want bread, baked crispy French bread is a perfect sidekick. Thank you for this recipe!

This dish turned out so well! I ended up doubling the recipe and saving the rest for a future week’s meal prep. I added about 3 cups more carrots and celery to incorporate more veggies. To decrease the fat content, I substituted butter with nonfat Greek yogurt at a 1:2 ratio (in place of 6 tablespoons of butter, I used 3 tablespoons of yogurt). I added a few dribbles of olive oil; the dish tasted no different than a buttered version. I added arrowroot starch in order to thicken the chowder.

Had to make on the stove because I ran out of time. Did not seem to hurt the recipe. My boys loved it. I added a lot more tomatoes (since they only come in 28 oz can) so I doubled the other ingredients except for the salt and cream mixture. Since I added a handful or so of wild rice, it got pretty thick on it's own. Very hearty, especially with the wild rice. Served with the cheesy garlic bread (also on this site). Great cold weather meal.

By sauteing the veggies (in the butter you're supposed to add later), and baking the fish, I was able to put this chowder together on the stove top in about 1/2hr. Didn't have wine or clam juice and it *still* came out yummy! Fish of the day was perch, and other than having to de-bone after baking, it was very, very tasty.

Great recipe I did as someone else suggested added the fish towards the end I also added some scallops it was very good next time I might add some old bay seasonings as well.when I added the flour mixture I used fat free half and half and put the crockpot on high for about an hour

This was sooo good! I made a few minor changes...made it on the stove top, added some diced potatoes and corn, just because I had some in the fridge, leftover. Also used half cod and half whiting, again because it's what I had on hand. It was a huge hit!

This was delicious! I used a bigger can of whole crushed tomoatoes (1 lb and 12 oz); at first I was worried but the tomatoes were easy to mash up when the stew was finished and the larger chunks of tomato added to the texture of the soup. I used halibut, and it was delicious but expensive. I will try it with cod next time. I was surprised the fish held up in the crock pot, and it was still delicious and tender. I waited to add the herbs until the last hour as well (I've heard long cooking can make herbs lose their flavor). I would definitely add the cream/butter/flour combo at the end. I used heavy cream, and it was a small price to pay for such a thick and delicious soup.
Loved it and added clams with the clam juice, for the fish I used Speckled sea trout that I caught (my first on artificial bait) so it was special.....will for sure make again!!!
I used cod and used Greek yogurt in place of Cream
I’m updating my last review. I added old bay seasoning And only added 1 pound of cod. I added shrimp the last 30 minutes. These updates read it five stars.??

I made it using Steelhead Trout and I doubled the recipe for my 7qt slow cooker. I used around 2lbs of trout and it was a little too much I thought. My family loves it though! I’ll definitely make it again
The soup was a hit with my husband. I added some ole bay and creole seasonings to give it some added flavor. He can't wait to have it again!
Fish too well done.
great simple what else can I tell you about it. it just good.

It was a very good chowder with an enticing aroma, but slightly on the bland side. Some salt, pepper and Sherry helped after the first couple of bites. I will definitely do it again, but experiment with some spices to add some depth - perhaps saffron.
No need to adjust anything, great as written
I made it to the recipe except for adding garlic and black pepper. DELICIOUS!

I made two change, I use coconut milk instead off light cream and a half a tea spoon pig lemon juice. We all had two servings. 

Delicious!
